title: a backwards list shuffle read one element past the live region before decrementing the count
object: the slab class's page list, a void* array grown by realloc in grow_slab_list
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a shuffle whose loop bound was decremented after the loop instead of before
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct malloc/calloc/realloc, with neither slabs.c nor cache.c between it and the request.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: 1.6.45:slabs.c carries the decrement BEFORE the loop (lines 758-761). The pre-fix order is at fa51ad8452d5^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow at the labelled probe on the buggy arm and is silent on the fixed arm -- keyed on heap-buffer-overflow, never on the string AddressSanitizer.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102458, with supervise resolving `expect mch_write_probe 0x102424` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- this is not a slab chunk and not a cache.c object -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the defect is an ORDERING, not an expression: the loop body and bound are both correct, and the fix only moves the decrement above the loop. It is also the one row here whose crossed array is the slab allocator's own BOOKKEEPING -- grown by plain realloc -- rather than storage the slab allocator hands out, which is what keeps the row plain rather than nested.
